title: Bacterial Blight of Cotton or Angular leaf spot of cotton

Header: Bacterial Blight of Cotton or Angular leaf spot of cotton

Prevention: Keep the canopy as open as possible to reduce humidity and promote drying of the foliage.
Do not cultivate or move equipment through fields when foliage is wet.
Plant high-quality, disease free, resistant, acid delinted seed.
Shred stalks and incorporate cotton debris.
Continue to irrigate as needed to meet crop demands, but do not over-irrigate.
Maintain good insect control to minimize the possibility of infection through wound.
Lush, rank foliage will contribute to higher humidity in the canopy, a longer period of leaf wetness, and will enhance infection.
Bury stubble rather than minimum tillage practices.
Rotate the crops preferably with corn, grain sorghum, peanut and soybean.
Crop rotation for one or more years will help control this disease.
Monitoring: The cotton variety, seed lot and a rating as to disease severity should be determined.
Scout fields and identify infected plants and varieties.
Check for infected leaves that have angular, dark-green water-soaked spots with a red to brown margin that will eventually turn dark-brown or black due to death of the infected tissues.
Disease can be spread by equipment or people moving through the field when the leaves are wet.
Avoid running ground rigs through or scouting fields when the foliage is still wet.
Direct Control: Once cotton has been deemed to be infected by the bacterium there are no curative measures that can be taken.
Restrictions: Spray when disease symptoms appear immediately.
